title: New Tremor Hits La Guaira, Venezuela, Reactivating Alerts
seoTitle: New Tremor Hits La Guaira, Venezuela
subtitle: Coastal state, already affected by June earthquakes, registered a 4.0 magnitude quake on the morning of August 18, 2026.
excerpt: A magnitude 4.0 tremor shook the coastal state of La Guaira, Venezuela, on the morning of August 18, 2026.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
A magnitude 4.0 tremor shook the coastal state of La Guaira, Venezuela, on the morning of Tuesday, August 18, 2026. The event reignited alerts in the region, which had already been severely affected by a double earthquake last June.

Details of the tremor and perception

According to information from the Venezuelan Foundation for Seismological Research (Funvisis), the telluric movement occurred exactly at 3:07 AM, local time. The epicenter was located 10 kilometers northwest of La Guaira, with a depth of 10 kilometers. The tremor was strongly felt by citizens in several areas of the country, including the capital, Caracas.

Authorities' response

Venezuela's acting president, Delcy Rodríguez, reported through her official channels that, so far, there were no reports of any kind of affected individuals. She also clarified that the Protection System was immediately activated to monitor and follow up on the situation.

Context: the June catastrophe

This new seismic event occurs almost two months after the catastrophe of June 24, 2026, when a double earthquake of magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5 devastated the north-central part of the country. La Guaira was one of the most affected areas, with dozens of buildings collapsing. The recent tremor revives the anguish of a population that has not yet fully recovered.

Balance of the previous tragedy

According to the latest official report released on Monday by the president of Parliament, Jorge Rodríguez, the total number of fatalities from the June tragedy rose to 6,438 people, after the confirmation of 137 new deaths in the last week. The balance also indicates that a total of 86,358 people required hospital care and 6,462 citizens were rescued alive.

Housing and humanitarian situation

The housing emergency remains critical in the affected zone. Authorities evaluated 59,109 homes, of which 10,696 are at “high risk” or uninhabitable. Despite the government's promise to deliver 4,000 homes before the end of the year, only 335 homes have been delivered so far. Thousands of displaced people continue to live in temporary camps under precarious conditions. The humanitarian situation was further complicated by torrential rains recorded last Sunday morning, which destroyed the tents of several families in Caracas.

Reconstruction and vigilance

Experts estimate that the total reconstruction will exceed 12 billion dollars, equivalent to 10.9% of the country's GDP. Meanwhile, rescue teams and civilian volunteers remain on alert, closely monitoring any aftershocks or new quakes on the sensitive Venezuelan coast.

With information from El Colombiano.
